artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Steven Wilson’s debut solo album Insurgentes, released in 2008 on Kscope, marks a pivotal moment in his career, distinct from his work with Porcupine Tree and other collaborative projects. Recorded in studios across the globe—from Mexico City to Japan and Israel—the album showcases Wilson’s experimental approach, blending elements of rock, ambient, industrial, and post-punk. Tracks range from melancholic ballads to atmospheric soundscapes and abrasive noise, reflecting Wilson’s diverse influences, including new wave, 4AD-era bands, and progressive rock. The album’s title references Avenida de los Insurgentes in Mexico City, where part of the recording took place, and its cinematic, textural quality sets it apart from Wilson’s later, more traditionally progressive solo releases.

Insurgentes occupies a unique space in Wilson’s discography as his first official solo album under his own name, signaling a departure from the expectations of band projects and allowing for greater creative freedom. While it shares some sonic territory with Porcupine Tree, its experimental nature and genre-blurring style distinguish it as a personal artistic statement. The album received positive critical attention for its ambition and originality, with reviewers noting its dark, introspective mood and its place alongside experimental works by artists like Thom Yorke and Nine Inch Nails. Though not a commercial blockbuster, Insurgentes established Wilson as a formidable solo artist and laid the groundwork for his subsequent solo explorations.
